title: Hans Kammler's Skoda Works saucer projects

tellings.quote: you do have real documented evidence that Hans Comler was running this thing called SCOD works in from 1942 to 45
we do know SS officer Hans Kammler probably ran a secret weapons unit for the Nazis called Skoda Works, which you can think of as the German Skunk Works.
tellings.difference: Calls it the German Skunk Works, adds Brno, says Kammler 'probably' ran it and credits Nick Cook's The Hunt for Zero Point.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Hans Kammler running the secret Skoda Works weapons unit in the 1940s, at Pilsen and Breslau/Wroclaw.

plain: From 1942 to 1945, the story goes, Hans Kammler, an officer in the SS, the Nazi party's own armed force, ran a secret weapons unit called the Skoda Works, which is tied in the telling to German work on saucer-shaped craft. Michels brings this up himself, saying there is "real documented evidence" for it in a book by the writer Tom Agoston about Kammler and in US Air Force documents. In another episode he is more careful, saying Kammler "probably" ran it, calling it "the German Skunk Works" (after the American aircraft maker Lockheed's secret design shop), and pointing to the journalist Nick Cook's book The Hunt for Zero Point. If it is true, the Nazis were building secret advanced craft during the war.
